units.title: Ancient Indian Wall Paintings

units.title: Jain and Pala Miniature Paintings

units.title: Mughal School of Painting
units.topics: Critical study of the development of Mughal painting under royal patronage during the reigns of:  Humayun  Akbar  Jahangir  Shah Jahan focusing on Persian influence, naturalism, portraiture, court scenes, and artists’ contributions.

units.title: Rajput School of Painting

units.title: Pahari School of Painting

units.title: Impressionism

units.title: Cybercrime and Cyber Law
units.topics: • Understanding Cybercrime: Exploration of various cyber offenses such as hacking, identity theft, financial fraud, and cyberbullying. • Legal Frameworks: Study of national and international laws addressing cybercrime, including the Information Technology Act and its implications. • Case Studies: Analysis of real-world cybercrime incidents to understand legal proceedings and enforcement challenges.

units.title: Social Media and E-Commerce Security
units.topics: • Social Media Risks: Identification of threats like phishing, impersonation, and data breaches on platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. • E-Commerce Vulnerabilities: Examination of security issues in online shopping and digital payment systems, including fraud prevention measures. • Best Practices: Guidelines for secure usage of social media and e-commerce platforms, emphasizing privacy settings and transaction safety.

units.title: Unit
units.topics: Digital Devices Security and Cyber security Tools ## p20 • Device Protection: Strategies for securing computers, smartphones, and its devices against malware and unauthorized access. • Cyber security Tools: Introduction to antivirus software, firewalls, encryption technologies, and multi-factor authentication methods. • Emerging Technologies: Overview of advanced cyber security solutions like AI-driven threat detection and block chain-based security protocols.

units.title: Exploring Historical Sites and Museums
units.topics: • Objective: Investigate the role of historical sites and museums in preserving and presenting art and cultural heritage. • Focus Areas: o Analyze the architecture and design of museums and galleries. o Study the curation and display methods employed in exhibitions. o Examine the impact of these institutions on public engagement with art.

units.title: Art Centers, Artist Studios, and Art Fairs
units.topics: • Objective: Examine the function and influence of art centers, artist studios, and art fairs on contemporary art practice. • Focus Areas: o Explore the collaborative environment of art centers and their role in fostering creativity. o Investigate how artist studios contribute to the development of individual artistic styles. o Assess the significance of art fairs in promoting artists and connecting them with audiences.

units.title: Biannual Exhibitions and Art Competitions
units.topics: • Objective: Analyze the role of biannual exhibitions and art competitions in the professional development of artists. • Focus Areas: o Study the themes and selection processes of major art competitions. o Evaluate the opportunities these events provide for exposure and career advancement. o Investigate the impact of such events on the art market and public perception of art.

units.title: Physical Fitness, Wellness & Lifestyle
units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Understanding the significance of maintaining physical fitness and wellness for overall health and quality of life. • Components of Physical Fitness: o Cardiovascular Endurance: The ability of the heart and ## p30 lungs to supply oxygen during sustained physical activity. o Muscular Strength: The maximum amount of force a muscle or group of muscles can generate. o Muscular Endurance: The ability of a muscle to continue to perform without fatigue. o Flexibility: The range of motion available at a joint. o Body Composition: The proportion of fat and non-fat mass in the body. • Components of Wellness: o Physical Wellness: Regular physical activity and proper nutrition. o Emotional Wellness: Understanding and managing feelings. o Social Wellness: Developing a sense of connection and belonging. o Intellectual Wellness: Engaging in creative and stimulating mental activities. o Spiritual Wellness: Seeking meaning and purpose in human existence.

units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Yoga is a mind-body practice that combines physical postures, breathing exercises, and meditation to promote overall health and well-being. • Elements of Yoga: o Asanas: Physical postures that improve flexibility, strength, and balance. o Pranayama: Breathing techniques that enhance respiratory function and mental clarity. o Meditation: Mental exercises that promote relaxation and mindfulness. • Introduction to Key Asanas: o Sukhasana: Easy Pose, promotes relaxation and meditation. o Tadasana: Mountain Pose, improves posture and balance. o Padmasana: Lotus Pose, enhances meditation and flexibility. o Shashankasana: Rabbit Pose, stretches the spine and calms the mind. o Naukasana: Boat Pose, strengthens the core and improves digestion. o Vrikshasana: Tree Pose, enhances balance and concentration. o Garudasana: Eagle Pose, improves focus and balance ## p31

units.title: ntroduction to Human Rights and Duties
units.topics: • Human Values: Understanding the significance of dignity, liberty, equality, justice, unity in diversity, ethics, and morals. • Human Rights Education: Meaning and importance of educating individuals on human rights to foster a just society. • Rights and Duties: The interrelationship between inherent, inalienable, and universal rights for individuals and groups, and the corresponding duties.

units.title: Legal Instruments and Terminology
units.topics: • Legal Instruments: Definition and significance of binding legal instruments such as covenants, charters, declarations, treaties, conventions, protocols, executive orders, and statutes. • International Law: Understanding the role of various legal ## p32 documents in enforcing human rights.

units.title: United Nations and Human Rights
units.topics: • History of Human Rights: A brief history of human rights from international and national perspectives. • UN Provisions: Overview of the United Nations Charter and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights, and duties and limitations. • Final Provisions: A look at the final provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

units.title: A student study tour is a trip taken by a group of students for
units.topics: educational purposes, often focusing on a specific subject or area of study.

units.title: These tours can take place locally, nationally, or even internationally,
units.topics: and offer students a chance to experience learning in a more immersive and interactive way, often outside the traditional classroom setting.

units.title: Exploring Historical Sites and Museums
units.topics: • Objective: Investigate the role of historical sites and museums in preserving and presenting art and cultural heritage. • Focus Areas: o Analyze the architecture and design of museums and galleries. o Study the curation and display methods employed in exhibitions. o Examine the impact of these institutions on public engagement with art.

units.title: Art Centers, Artist Studios, and Art Fairs
units.topics: • Objective: Examine the function and influence of art centers, artist studios, and art fairs on contemporary art practice. • Focus Areas: o Explore the collaborative environment of art centers and their role in fostering creativity. o Investigate how artist studios contribute to the development of individual artistic styles. o Assess the significance of art fairs in promoting artists and connecting them with audiences. ## p35

units.title: Biannual Exhibitions and Art Competitions
units.topics: • Objective: Analyze the role of biannual exhibitions and art competitions in the professional development of artists. • Focus Areas: o Study the themes and selection processes of major art competitions. o Evaluate the opportunities these events provide for exposure and career advancement. o Investigate the impact of such events on the art market and public perception of art.
